source_quote: The Business IT Management program combines business and information technology
answer: The Business IT Management program combines business and IT so students understand how IT and computer applications improve business effectiveness and efficiency, covering databases, programming, networking, telecommunications, e-commerce and online development. It requires 99 credits.

source_quote: The mandatory Business IT Management program courses are listed in the table below.
answer: BITM mandatory courses: BADM 485 Co-op Work Experience, BADM 490 Entrepreneurship, BITM 305 Introduction to Programming, BITM 310 Database Management Systems, BITM 340 Development Tools of Information Systems, BITM 355 Networking, BITM 415 Business Intelligence, BITM 450 Big Data Analytics, BMGT 300 Project Management, and a 3-credit Major Elective.

source_quote: the student must study 3 credit hours of major electives. Major electives could be upper-
answer: BITM students take 3 credits of major electives, e.g., BACC 350, BADM 480, BITM 320 Enterprise Resource Planning, BITM 402 Advanced Web Programming, BITM 410 Advanced Programming and Data Structures, or BITM 455 Advanced Networking.

source_quote: job opportunities for people with skills in online sales, electronic market research, e-
answer: BITM graduates find jobs in the MENA region in online sales, electronic market research, e-commerce, online transaction security, mobile application development and information systems management, in areas like telemarketing, e-government and social media.

source_quote: Use ICT tools and programs to enhance performance and improve
answer: BITM outcomes: apply business knowledge in problem-solving; use ICT tools to improve business efficiency; communicate effectively in English; analyze business problems and propose solutions; and respond to ethical dilemmas per codes of conduct.

source_quote: Each student must complete 8 weeks of practical training in a field related to their
answer: BITM students complete 8 weeks of Co-op training (BADM 485), usually in the summer of the third year, with faculty follow-up, reports, posters and presentations; ENGL 217 and Senior Standing are prerequisites.
